children: The initiative will cover 201 clusters across 303 mandals and 5,869 villages, with private investment targeted at Rs 60,000 crore

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu and Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Friday laid the foundation stone for a global horticulture hub at Madanapalle, with the project estimated to involve Rs 1 lakh crore in investment. They also laid the foundation stone for the Indian School of Agriculture (ISA), which will focus on technology, research and innovation in agriculture.

The horticulture hub will be developed in three phases, with the TDP-led NDA government contributing Rs 40,352 crore towards the project. The state government will seek to mobilise another Rs 60,000 crore from private-sector investments, according to an official release.

The project will cover Anantapur, Annamayya, Chittoor, Kurnool, Nandyal, Sri Sathya Sai, Tirupati, Kadapa, Prakasam and Markapuram districts. Development works will be undertaken through 201 clusters spread across 303 mandals and 5,869 villages in these 10 districts.

The government plans to expand the existing horticulture cultivation area of 8.41 lakh hectares by another six lakh hectares. This will take the total cultivation area covered under the plan to 14.41 lakh hectares across the identified districts.

The project aims to increase horticultural production from the current 222 lakh metric tonnes to 435 lakh metric tonnes. According to the release, the initiative is expected to directly benefit around 9.6 lakh farmers across the 10 districts.

The Indian School of Agriculture will be modelled on the Indian School of Business and will focus on agricultural development through modern technology, research and innovation. Reliance Industries Limited has come forward to work with the state government in establishing and managing the institution.

The ISA will provide technology-driven guidance to farmers and develop solutions for key agricultural challenges. Its focus areas will include digital agriculture, precision farming, crop monitoring, smart irrigation and market intelligence, among other activities.
